A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same ProtoMM research, with corresponding text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. Neither contains an appendix; both mention separate Supplementary Material that is not included in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProtoMM classification experiments across 15 datasets, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, transport-plan visualizations and inference-time measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, visualizations and timing measurements in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same distributed features, multimodal prototypes, importance weighting, optimal-transport prediction and visual-cache updates. Changing 'Proto' to 'ProtoMM' in Table 4 only corrects the method name.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 classification datasets and four ImageNet distribution-shift variants: ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNetV2 and ImageNet-Sketch. No evaluated domain, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2 and 4, including TPT, DiffTPT, TDA, DOTA, DPE and AWT. The bibliography additions and removals do not change the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain RN50 and ViT-B/16 backbones, streaming evaluation, accuracy and average-accuracy metrics, 50 visual and textual augmentations, top-S of 25 and threshold 0.8. The ablation and timing protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The module ablation in Table 3, augmentation-count analysis in Figure 4, threshold and selection-size analyses in Figures 5–6, and transport-plan examples in Figure 7 are unchanged. The prototype-discrepancy comparison in Figure 2 is also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. There is no change in statistical or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical entries, and the figures retain their reported findings. For example, Table 1 ProtoMM averages remain 63.10% for RN50 and 70.70% for ViT-B/16; Table 4 retains 21 minutes and 63.76% accuracy.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including discrete distribution definitions, transport constraints, entropy regularization, importance weights and the prototype-update rule, are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free dynamic multimodal prototypes and optimal transport. The claimed evaluation across 15 datasets and 1.03% average improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of prototype accumulation, augmentation saturation, confidence-filtering failures, transport heatmaps and runtime tradeoffs. The conclusion retains the same future directions concerning efficiency and higher-level image/video tasks.

D1.justification: Implementation details remain unchanged, including GPT-3.5 descriptions, augmentation procedures, hyperparameters and the NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. The new acknowledgment credits USTC computing support but adds no technical specifications, reproduction procedure or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds two Xun Yang et al. works on hierarchical visual transformation and contrastive cross-modality video question answering, cited in the introduction as references 51–52. It removes v1's EVA-CLIP and Sigmoid loss for language image pre-training entries. The substantive positioning against prior methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 6, 'Acknowledge,' corrects 'Proto' to 'ProtoMM' in Table 4, and updates citation numbering and version text. The scientific prose and Sections 1–5 otherwise retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment and bibliography edits cause limited text reflow across pages 9–11, and Table 4 has a corrected method label. Figures 1–7, table structures, captions and scientific-content placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Table 4 label correction, limited reference changes and acknowledgment provide small editorial and attribution updates. The method, experimental evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
